text:
jess: Heads up — hit-rate for prefix/KV cache tanked on RAG-chat traffic after yesterday's kernel swap. Seen ~78% -> ~32% on a couple customer workloads. Posting quick profiler output and a suspected keying snippet.

mohan: ugh. which kernel swap? the attention microkernel change?

jess: yes, swapped to fast_attn_v2 on a subset of pods (pool-b). Deploy bot shows 2026-03-16T22:03 deploy. Perf profile: 
```
sampled_requests: 3k
workload: rag-chat (multi-turn)
old_kv_hit: 0.78
new_kv_hit: 0.32
avg_latency_p50: 48ms -> 62ms
tokens_per_request: 120
prefix_sharing_rate: high (lots of same system + doc prefixes)
```

elena: do we have diffs for the cache key generation? any truncation or hash salt changes?

jess: grabbing snippet from runtime that generates the cache key (production simplified):
```
key = f"model:{model_name}|prompt_hash:{sha1(normalize(prompt))[:16]}|len:{len(tokens)}"
```
We noticed normalize() is whitespace/case folding only. fast_attn_v2 seems to change tokenization boundaries for certain unicode and punctuation -> len(tokens) sometimes differs by +/-1 which changes the key. That explains misses across mixed pod pools.

mohan: ah so same raw text -> different tokenization -> different len -> different key => cache miss. Are we including tokenizer version in the key?

jess: nope. We include model_name but not tokenizer/version or kernel. The risky part: kernel influences tokenization via internal subword handling in our fused tokenizer path.

ryan: for the record, completions traffic didn't drop, right?

jess: completions: hit stayed ~76% -> 70% (small drop), but the effect is much worse for multi-turn chat + RAG because we rely on shared prefixes (system prompt + doc snippets) and many requests that formerly collapsed to same key are now split.

elena: options: 1) include tokenizer checksum + kernel id in cache key namespace, 2) normalize tokenization outputs before keying (e.g., use canonical token ids for prefix), 3) revert kernel on pool-b until we have migration strategy.

mohan: agree. Also we should avoid using len(tokens) as a key fragment if it flips with minor tokenization changes. Maybe include token_hash based on token ids instead of len.

jess: quick micro-bench: patched key to use sha1(token_ids)[:12] + tokenizer_version. Results on staging: 
```
old_key_hitrate (fast_attn_v2): 0.33
new_key_hitrate (token-id-hash + tokenz_v1): 0.81
p50 latency: 60ms -> 46ms
```
So using token-id-hash solves cross-kernel collisions.

ryan: nice. any perf cost for computing token-id-hash? hashing token ids every request could add CPU.

jess: measured ~0.8ms extra on p50 for small prompts, but we save 12-15ms from cache hits — net win. For high-throughput short completions it might not pay off.

elena: then we need workload-specific keying policy. Chat/RAG: use token-id-hash + tokenizer_version + namespace=chat. Short single-turn completions: keep cheap key (prompt_hash + model). We can set this via routing config or per-route annotations.

mohan: also consider warmup strategies: when a session is created, prefetch likely prefixes (system + last doc chunks) into local pool cache to avoid cold misses on first few messages. For RAG we can prefetch top-k doc prefixes used by retrieval.

jess: sketched a warmup patch: on session open, call /internal/prefetch with list of doc prefix token-id hashes. Prefetch runs async and populates local KV. Implement heuristics: only for routes with >20ms read latency and avg tokens>50.

ryan: I like prefetch + separate namespaces. Also add a toggle to force stable-tokenizer mode during kernel rollout (force old tokenizer behavior) as a short term mitigation.

elena: we should also update tooling to record tokenizer_version and kernel_id on traces and cost dashboards so we can slice hitrates by those dims. Currently dashboards only show model + route.

jess: added to TODOs. Also we found one more gotcha: structured output pipelines (we append a JSON schema suffix) sometimes vary whitespace inside examples; normalize_schema_examples fixed a batch of misses. Example: previously two prompts with same schema but different example spacing hashed differently. Fix: canonicalize example blocks before keying.

mohan: what about long-context sessions? If tokenized prefix is >cache_prefix_limit we currently truncate token-id lists before hashing which made collisions when truncation boundary changed. We should compute hash over a stable sliding window anchored to the start tokens (system + first doc chunk) and include truncation_strategy in key.

jess: agreed. changed key to include truncation_strategy=anchor_0_len256. Regression tests added.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-16T22:03 -> pool-b fast_attn_v2 (rollout 30%) :white_check_mark:

ryan: action items: 
- revert fast_attn_v2 rollout on pool-b OR deploy token-id-hash keying ASAP (mohan)
- add tokenizer_version + kernel_id tags to traces (elena)
- implement per-workload keying policies + warmup prefetch (jess)
- update dashboards to slice by tokenizer/kernel (ryan)

jess: I'll open PRs for token-id-hash (small change) and warmup endpoint. Putting a tentative revert if we don't get a staged fix in 2 hours.

mohan: I'll instrument a canary that computes both old and new keys and emits mismatch stats to help validate. low overhead.

elena: also let's not forget docs for operators: note that kernel swaps can imply tokenizer differences — add to playbook.

jess: thanks — will follow up with PR links and staging numbers. :thumbsup:
